sections.title: 1. Executive Summary
blocks: US-4222 describes updating an agency. We tested it against the real staging system, on a real agency record (AGN2 — Test Egypt), and the feature works: of the 37 test cases you approved, 31 passed. Agency details, owner details, payment settings, documents, the logo, product selection and the submit-for-approval workflow all behave as the story describes.

Two things need your attention. A file that is not a PDF is accepted and stored as an agency contract document — the system checks neither the contents nor even the file name extension, although the logo upload beside it does check both. And deselecting a product cannot be undone: re-selecting it demands supplier-credential details the agency never had, so the form will not save. We found the second one by doing it, which means one change is still outstanding on the record — the Flight product remains deselected on AGN2, and putting it back needs a decision from you.

Three cases could not be run at all, for one reason: the installation has a single login, so an update cannot be submitted by one person and approved by another. That is the separation the approval workflow exists to enforce, and it is the one part of US-4222 we cannot tell you anything about.
16 of the 53 designed cases were not authorized to run — you rejected them at review — so this report covers 69.8% of the designed suite.

sections.title: 2. Outcome figures — both denominators

items: Executable scope (Review = Approved): 37 cases — Passed 31 (83.8%) · Failed 1 (2.7%) · Blocked 4 (10.8%) · Skipped 1 (2.7%) · Not Executed 0 · Inconclusive 0.
Not authorized to run this pass: 16 cases, all Rejected at Review (30.2% of the suite). Reported, not dropped.
Suite total: 53 designed cases. Authorized Coverage: 69.8% (37 of 53).

blocks: The ring and the six status cards above are computed over the executable scope, which is the pass rate's denominator. The Suite Total card is the full designed suite. Both figures are shown because a pass rate quoted against the suite total understates the run, and quoted against the suite total without saying so it overstates coverage.

items.body: Deselecting a product is irreversible through the UI, and it destroys the product's supplier-credential configuration. Re-selecting Flight renders a blank supplier-credential panel in which Manager Name and Supplier Credentials Description are mandatory, and the form refuses to save until both are filled — the agency has no values for either. The stored credential is still present in the grid and its selection checkbox is still ticked, so the association was never lost; the block is purely the empty panel.

fields.label: Suspected Component
fields.value: Select Product / supplier-credential panel on the Update Agency form

fields.label: Layer
fields.value: Frontend — the block is client-side form validation on a panel the client itself renders empty

fields.label: Reproducibility
fields.value: Always — four independent attempts, each refused with the same two Required markers: plain re-select and save; re-select with a wait for the section to repopulate; re-select with the stored credential row explicitly ticked; and clicking the stored row to load it into the panel

fields.label: Regression
fields.value: Unknown — no earlier execution of this case exists to compare against

fields.label: Impact
fields.value: An administrator who deselects a product by mistake cannot undo it. Restoring the product requires inventing supplier-credential details the agency never had, which replaces one wrong state with another, or a direct database correction. On a live agency this silently changes what the agency is able to sell.

fields.label: Root cause (inferred, not established)
fields.value: The credential panel appears to be an "add a credential" form whose validators activate once the product group is marked dirty, rather than a view of the credential already attached. That would explain why the record saved normally for the whole run while the product selection was untouched, and refuses only after the selection is changed.

fields.label: Confidence
fields.value: High — reproduced four ways, with the refusal message located and attributed to two named fields each time

items.evidence: manual_execution/artifacts/TC-AGENCY-041.png (the product deselected and persisted) · ManualExecutionResults.md §5 (per-case record, including all four restoration attempts)

items.body: Agency contract documents are subject to no format validation whatsoever: not by content, and not even by file extension, since the file dialog is unrestricted. A 297-byte plain-text file with no %PDF header, named .pdf, was accepted silently, submitted, approved, and listed as an attached contract document after the agency was reopened.

fields.label: Layer
fields.value: Frontend and Backend — the browser accepted it with no filter and the server stored it, so neither layer validates

fields.label: Reproducibility
fields.value: Unable to confirm — observed once in this run. The single observation was clean and fully evidenced, but the standard for Always is at least two independent observations.

fields.label: Regression
fields.value: Unknown — no earlier execution of this case exists to compare against

fields.label: Impact
fields.value: Any file can be stored as an agency contract document provided it is named .pdf. A user who attaches the wrong file, or a corrupt one, receives no indication of the problem; the error surfaces later, when somebody opens the contract and finds it unreadable. Because the stored artefact is the evidence of the commercial agreement with the agency, the failure is discovered exactly when the document matters most.

fields.label: Root cause (inferred, not established)
fields.value: The logo control constrains its file dialog with accept="image/*" and rejects a non-image at submit, while the document control declares no accept and produced no message. The most plausible explanation is that document format validation was simply never implemented, rather than implemented and bypassed.

fields.label: Confidence
fields.value: High that the behaviour is as described; the observation is direct and the stored result was re-read after reopening the record.

items.evidence: manual_execution/artifacts/TC-AGENCY-020.png — the accepted file listed after reopening

items.body: AC-2 Agency Owner Details · AC-4 Agency Logo · AC-5 Wonder Travel Sales Contact · AC-8 Product Access / Agency Features · AC-10 Import PNR Option — all approved cases in these groups executed and passed.
AC-1 Agency Master fields (6 of 7 approved cases executed) · AC-7 Payment settings (5 of 6) · No-acceptance-criterion workflow group (3 of 6). The rest were Blocked or Deferred.
AC-3 Upload Document Details — at least one approved case failed; see the Defect Register (TC-AGENCY-020).

AC-6 Bank Account Details — every case covering it was rejected at review, a decision recorded in the Coverage Report §11.2 and accepted there. AC-9 Airline Supplier Credential (PCC) — same. Both are listed rather than omitted because a missing row reads as "nothing to say", which is the opposite of the truth.

ASM-012 — the Mandatory marking on document and logo describes create-time only, not a re-upload on every update. An agency with an existing document and logo was updated without touching either section, and both remained attached.
FINDING-005 — Outstanding Threshold is a later enhancement, mandatory, with an unconfirmed valid range. The field accepted 10 against an observed 5; no constraint was encountered at that value.
FINDING-007 — a single credential prevents maker/checker separation from being tested. All three approval cases remain Blocked for exactly this reason.

Reviewer-reported rule: the agency name accepts letters, digits and underscore only. "QA Test Agency" was accepted and redisplayed with its space intact. The reported rule does not hold for the space character, which matters because the agency's own stored name contains one.

ASM-016 — changing Branch may overwrite Product Access and Sales Contact. Deferred; requires a dedicated environment. TC-AGENCY-041 gave the deferral concrete support: a product change on this form could not be undone.

Approval by a second user could not be tested. The installation has one credential (odeysysadmin, Super Admin), so submitter and approver are the same identity. The approval workflow's central control — that somebody else approves — is unverified. Everything upstream of it is verified.

One environment change remains outstanding. The application will not save a re-selected product without supplier-credential values the agency never held. The record is not identical to its pre-run state; AGN2 is currently missing the Flight product.
Branch re-inheritance not exercised — deferred by the case's own notes as potentially destructive on a shared environment. ASM-016 remains open.

One case is blocked for automation only. The payment-option checkboxes cannot be driven reliably through the public UI: the visible controls read unchecked while the underlying model still carried a selection, confirmed by network capture. No consequence for the application — the behaviour was verified manually and is correct. The limitation is the harness's.
16 designed cases were not authorized — Rejected at Review. 30.2% of the designed suite is unexamined this pass, by decision rather than by omission.

Product Access supplier rows changed mid-run, not by this run. The read-only supplier list changed from SalamAir/FlyNas to Sabre between two clean verifications. Recorded, not corrected — overwriting it would have destroyed somebody else's configuration.

sections.title: 7. Cleanup / follow-up
sections.heading: Outstanding change left on the environment (1):

items.label: Needs a data decision
items.body: The Flight product remains deselected. Restoring it means either supplying the two supplier-credential values through the UI — which adds data the agency did not previously hold — or restoring the product association directly in the database. This is a data decision, not a QA one.
Decide how to restore the Flight product on AGN2 — through the UI with invented credential values, or directly in the database.
Treat the irreversibility as a defect in its own right: re-selecting a product should restore it without demanding credential details that were never required to remove it.
Validate document uploads at least as strictly as logo uploads already are — the logo control's accept attribute and its format check are the working model, on the same form.
Provide a second, non-Super-Admin credential with approval rights so maker/checker separation can be tested. This is the single change that would unblock the most coverage.
Schedule on a dedicated environment where Branch re-inheritance can be exercised without risking live data.
Rotate the odeysysadmin password now that the run is complete.

sections.title: 9. Delivery Completeness

items: Every test case in scope has a recorded outcome — all 53 suite cases appear, 37 with an execution outcome and 16 as Excluded.
Every Failed/Inconclusive case meets the Defect Documentation Standard in full — TC-AGENCY-020, plus TC-AGENCY-041 documented to the same standard despite passing.
Every result's evidence captured, or its absence stated with a reason.
CSV has one row per test case in scope, statuses unabbreviated — 53 rows.
Coverage computed from the Traceability Matrix; uncovered requirements shown as not verified.
All four renderings — Results, Summary, CSV, and this report — agree on every test case's status: they are generated from one result set in a single pass, so they cannot diverge.
No script of any kind was produced as an artifact. The execution harness was scratchpad scaffolding and is deleted.
